quiz_title: AP CS A - Day 12 Exit Quiz: Object Equality & Null References
topic: Comparing Object References (== vs .equals()), Null Reference, NullPointerException, and Short-Circuit Defensive Guarding

questions.question: Consider the following code segment. What is printed as a result of executing this code segment?
questions.explanation: Variables s1 and s2 were instantiated using the new operator, so they refer to two distinct String objects at different memory addresses on the heap; therefore, s1 == s2 evaluates to false. Assigning s3 = s1 creates an alias pointing to the exact same object as s1, making s1 == s3 true. The .equals() method compares the sequence of characters, which are identical ("robot"), evaluating to true.

questions.question: Consider the following code segment where str is a String variable initialized to null. What happens when this code segment executes?
options: A NullPointerException is thrown at runtime
The code does not compile because null cannot be compared to a String
questions.explanation: In Java, null indicates that a reference variable does not point to an object in memory. Attempting to invoke an instance method such as .equals() on a null reference causes the Java Virtual Machine to throw a NullPointerException at runtime.

questions.question: A programmer wants to check if a String variable input is not null and contains the word "exit". Which of the following code segments correctly uses short-circuit evaluation to safely perform this check without risking a NullPointerException?
questions.explanation: In if (input != null && input.equals("exit")), if input is null, the left condition input != null evaluates to false. Because of short-circuit evaluation in logical AND (&&), Java immediately terminates evaluation of the expression and never executes input.equals("exit"), safely avoiding a NullPointerException.

questions.question: Consider the following method. What is the return value of checkMembership("Gold", new String("Gold"))?
questions.explanation: tier1 refers to a String literal in the string pool, while tier2 is instantiated explicitly using new String("Gold"), placing it in a different heap location. Because they reside at different memory addresses, tier1 == tier2 evaluates to false. Execution proceeds to the else if condition where tier1.equals(tier2) compares their characters, evaluating to true and returning "Matching Content".

questions.question: Consider the following code segment. Which of the following expressions is guaranteed to evaluate to true without throwing a NullPointerException, regardless of whether String variable code is null or initialized to "SECRET"?
questions.code: String code; // may be null or any String value
questions.explanation: Because the literal "SECRET" is guaranteed to be a non-null String object, calling the .equals() method on it is always safe. If code is null, "SECRET".equals(null) simply returns false without throwing an exception. In contrast, calling code.equals(...) when code is null causes a NullPointerException.
